flags: The triangular wave is continuous after the absolute value, despite the fractional-part jump; shared branch endpoints must be counted once.

routes.label: Count crossings of the triangular wave
Count crossings on the function's branches

question:
Let \(f(x) = |2\{x\} - 1|\) where \(\{x\}\) denotes the fractional part of \(x.\) The number \(n\) is the smallest positive integer such that the equation \[nf(xf(x)) = x\] has at least \(2012\) real solutions \(x.\) What is \(n?\)

Note: the fractional part of \(x\) is a real number \(y = \{x\},\) such that \(0 \le y \lt 1\) and \(x - y\) is an integer.
solution:
For every integer \(m\), the graph of \(f\) joins \((m,1)\), \((m+\tfrac12,0)\), and \((m+1,1)\) by straight segments. Thus \(0\le f\le1\), and \(f\) is continuous even at integers: the fractional-part jump disappears after taking the absolute value.

Fix a positive integer \(n\). Every solution satisfies \(0\le x\le n\). The endpoint \(x=0\) is not a solution, while \(x=n\) is, since \(f(n)=1\). Define
\[
g(x)=xf(x),
\qquad H(x)=nf(g(x))-x.
\]
We will count the zeros of the continuous function \(H\) on each unit interval.

For \(j=0,1,\ldots,n-1\), the inner function has formulas
\[
g(x)=
\begin{cases}
x(2j+1-2x),&j\le x\le j+\tfrac12,\\
x(2x-2j-1),&j+\tfrac12\le x\le j+1.
\end{cases}
\]
For \(j\ge1\), the first piece decreases from \(j\) to \(0\). For every \(j\ge0\), the second increases from \(0\) to \(j+1\).

We also need to know that each crossing is unique. On either of these monotone pieces, if \(u<v\), expansion gives
\[
|g(v)-g(u)|
=(v-u)(2u+2v-2j-1)
\ge v-u.
\]
For the decreasing piece the last factor is at least \(2j-1\ge1\); for the increasing piece it is at least \(2j+1\ge1\).

Split each piece further whenever \(g(x)\) reaches an integer or a half-integer. On each resulting branch, \(f(g(x))\) moves strictly between \(0\) and \(1\). If it increases, its change between \(u\) and \(v\) is \(2|g(v)-g(u)|\), so
\[
H(v)-H(u)\ge(2n-1)(v-u)>0.
\]
If it decreases, \(H\) also strictly decreases. Thus \(H\) is strictly monotone on every such branch.

At a branch endpoint where \(f(g(x))=0\), we have \(H(x)=-x<0\). Where \(f(g(x))=1\), we have \(H(x)=n-x>0\), except at \(x=n\), where it is zero. Continuity and strict monotonicity therefore give exactly one zero on each branch, with the final branch contributing the endpoint \(x=n\).

For \(j\ge1\), the decreasing piece takes \(g\) from \(j\) to \(0\), crossing \(2j\) half-unit ranges. It contributes \(2j\) zeros. The increasing piece takes \(g\) from \(0\) to \(j+1\), crossing \(2j+2\) half-unit ranges and contributing \(2j+2\) zeros. Together these give \(4j+2\).

The initial piece \(0\le x\le\tfrac12\) is the exception to the monotonic description, but it contributes no zeros. Here
\[
0\le g(x)=\frac18-2\left(x-\frac14\right)^2\le\frac18,
\]
so \(f(g(x))\ge\tfrac34\). Hence \(nf(g(x))\ge\tfrac34>x\). The other half of \([0,1]\) contributes two zeros, again agreeing with \(4j+2\) when \(j=0\).

No shared branch endpoint is a zero except \(x=n\): the other endpoint values of \(H\) are strictly positive or negative. Thus there is no double counting, and the total number of distinct solutions is
\[
\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}(4j+2)=2n^2.
\]
Finally,
\[
2\cdot31^2=1922<2012,
\qquad
2\cdot32^2=2048\ge2012.
\]
Since \(2n^2\) increases for positive integers \(n\), the smallest possible value is \(\boxed{32}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
